main_body: Long wooden trough: brown rim around a recessed blue water surface, with a dark brown plank front face below
top_band: Brown back rim at rows 4-5, then the water surface as a light-to-mid blue band at rows 5-8, then a lighter brown front rim at rows 9-10
evidence: In a middle column the back rim (rows 4-5) leads into 4 rows of water (rows 5-8) that read as a horizontal surface seen from above, with a darker blue row at the front. The lighter brown front rim (rows 9-10) acts as the front-edge line, and a dark band at row 11 acts as the eave shadow. Below it a brown plank face runs rows 12-14. The water sits inside the rims, so the opening is visible. The water is a flat rectangle, not an ellipse, but it is clearly a surface, so the drawing is a valid 3/4 piece.

style.evidence: The water has about 3-4 blue steps, a faint grid pattern and a few sparkle pixels. The wood rims and front face have only 2-3 browns each. The front face is a large, almost flat dark-brown area with only a faint plank seam and no grain or per-board highlights. The outline is a dark brown-black that leans slightly brown, which is acceptable. Overall the piece is thinner and flatter than the roofed well and the cheese stall, whose tiles carry many more colours and texture dots. Many tiles here hold only 3-5 colours.
